newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen end down after machinery orders data.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen end down after machinery orders data.

text.p: An unexpected surge in Japan's machinery orders data depressed SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures on Tuesday.
Private sector machinery orders, excluding those for electric power firms and ships, rose a seasonally adjusted 13.6 percent for July, after a fall of 9.6 percent in June.
Bank of Japan (BOJ)'s drainage of 100 billion yen from the money market, against expectations of a neutral stance, also weighed on both ends of the Japanese yield curve, as did gains in Tokyo stocks.
But dealers said BOJ governor Yasuo Matsushita's statement that Japan's economic recovery was not yet sustainable gave a slight lift to the market.
"The only thing giving slight support to the market was the BOJ statement, which suggests they're maintaining a soft policy," said a dealer with a U.S. institution.
The most active March Euroyen contract finished at 99.09 against its CME close at 99.13. December JGBs ended at 121.30 against their previous 121.34.
Another trader said March Euroyen looked supported at 99.05, with resistance near its previous high of 99.18.
Eurodollar futures ended scarcely changed in thin trade, with March at 93.80, unchanged from the IMM close.
Dealers said last Friday's U.S. August employment report, showing strong gains in wages coupled with a drop in the jobless rate, raised the spectre of inflation and a U.S. rate hike.

But players will scrutinise August wholesale and consumer inflation releases, due on Thursday and Friday respectively, for clearer indications of the Federal Reserve's expected stance at its September 24 meeting.
